clauses.reason: This clause, the amended Sections 1 and 2 and the opening of Section 3 of Executive Order 10587 as rewritten by Executive Order 11086, terminated on 1986-02-25 when EO 12553 revoked the order by number. Mechanism: express revocation by a numbered list ("Revocation of Various Executive Orders"; "any amendments thereto, are revoked:"); the target is identified by this row: "11086 Amending the administration of the Trading with the Enemy Act". The effective date is the signing date, 1986-02-25 (alternative: publication on 1986-03-03).

This clause, the remainder of Section 3 keeping jurisdiction over the organization's claims with the Attorney General pending their discharge, terminated on 1986-02-25 when EO 12553 revoked the order by number (same row and effective date as the first clause). Its own contingent ending, discharge of the claims, is not evidenced by any held source and is disclosed as open rather than claimed.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (28 FR 1833) prints Executive Order 11086 as an order of the President (John F. Kennedy) dated 1963-02-26; the number, subject and date agree with the census register row (subject: Amendment of Executive Order No. 10587 relating to the administration of section 32(h) of the Trading with the Enemy Act). I read the whole text and signature block. Inventory: the dossier's two clauses, the amendments of Sections 1 and 2 and the opening of Section 3, and the remainder of Section 3, are contiguous and together cover every operative sentence; I confirm the inventory as complete. The order amends sections 1, 2 and 3 of Executive Order No. 10587 of January 13, 1955 (administration of section 32 of the Trading with the Enemy Act): Section 1 designates the Jewish Restitution Successor Organization as successor in interest to deceased persons for subsection (h) of section 32; Section 2 delegates to the Foreign Claims Settlement Commission the functions under subsection (n), including designating other organizations and paying $500,000 out of the War Claims Fund; and Section 3 keeps jurisdiction over the claims filed by that organization with the Attorney General, pending discharge of those claims, as the second clause states. Ending: EO 12553 of February 25, 1986, titled "Revocation of Various Executive Orders", orders that the listed Executive Orders, and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" Its table lists this order by number and subject on one line: "11086 Amending the administration of the Trading with the Enemy Act". EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the held text was searched for effective, take effect, shall become, except, notwithstanding, nothing in, provided that and saving, with no hit outside table subjects); it is headed as an order of February 25, 1986 and signed that day, so the date is read as 1986-02-25, the signing date. The alternative reading is the Federal Register publication date, 1986-03-03 (Monday, March 3, 1986, 51 FR 7237); no later date is supported by the text. The quoted source for the end is the enacting paragraph of EO 12553, which names no order; the order is named by its row in the No./Subject table, quoted above, so the table row and the enacting paragraph are read together. The order amends EO 10587, and EO 12553's table also lists the number 10587 (the table's subjects for that page are separated from its numbers in the held OCR text, so this claim does not depend on matching that row). The second clause contains an own-terms contingent ending: the Attorney General's jurisdiction remains pending discharge of the organization's claims by its acceptance of payment or other discharge pursuant to law. No held source states that the claims were discharged or when, so that contingent ending is not evidenced; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-28 an unestablished earlier event is not claimed, and it is disclosed as open for the human reviewer. Savings: EO 12553 has no savings clause or exception; payments or designations already made are accrued consequences. Searches selected after reading their coverage notes (all three complete, no coverage warning): U.S. Code release point 119-121 (no hit for this order), eCFR as of 2026-10-14 (no hit), and the Federal Register catalog disposition notes (2 machine hits, the revocation note on this order and the matching note on EO 12553).

savings.reason: After a bounded search of the full text of EO 12553, the U.S. Code and eCFR (no hits for this order) and the Federal Register catalog notes, no savings clause or exception was found; designations and payments completed before the revocation are accrued consequences and no continuing independent command survives.
